title: [DONE] Fix CP/M write path: AddFile + FindFreeDirEntry + Rename ext + BlockMap reuse
description:
Critical findings from prior code-review session, all addressed in this session:

#8022: AddFile silently dropped data on the floor (only wrote dir entry, never allocated blocks or wrote content). Now: scans GetBlockMap for free blocks, writes content into them, builds 1+ directory entries (multi-extent for files >16 KB), pads tail with $1A.

#8023: FindFreeDirEntry was scanning boot tracks instead of directory area, used hardcoded 512-byte-sector geometry, single-track only, and required Filename to be all-$E5 (over-strict — standard CP/M deletion only sets User=$E5). Rewritten to use FDPB.OFF + TI.SectorSize, walk multiple tracks, accept any User=$E5 entry.

#8027: TCPMFileEntry.Rename updated FName but never FExt. Display became 'BAR.DAT.TXT' after rename. Now uses TCPMFileName.Parse to split.

Bonus fix: AddFile now also treats BlockMap=3 (deleted-but-referenced) as allocatable, matching CP/M's actual deletion semantics (block reuse after  marking).

Verified end-to-end via tests/test_cpm_write.pas (4 round-trips: 100 B, 4 KB, 17 KB multi-extent, 0 B empty). All pass byte-for-byte. 127/127 TUI regression tests still pass.
acceptance_criteria: All 4 round-trip tests pass. Production code reviewed.
close_reason: All 4 critical findings fixed and verified by 4-case round-trip test plus 127/127 TUI regression. See test_cpm_write.pas.

title: Resolve TInterfacedObject + class-ref double-free fragility
description:
TDiskBenderDSK and TDiskBenderCPM extend TInterfacedObject, so they auto-destroy when their interface refcount hits zero. But callers across the project hold them as raw class references (Disk: TDiskBenderDSK) AND pass them to consumers via interface (FS receives IVirtualDisk). When the consumer is freed the interface ref drops to 0, destroying the object — then the explicit Disk.Free is a use-after-free / double-free.

Hit this concretely in tests/test_cpm_write.pas during this session: AddFile passed, then crashed on Disk.Free. Fixed in the test by using IVirtualDisk var only and dropping explicit Free, but the underlying fragility lives across the project (uDSKLocation.pas:283-298, GUI code, CLI dispatch).

Choose one ownership model project-wide:
A) Drop TInterfacedObject inheritance, manage lifetime manually with class refs
B) Commit fully to interface refs everywhere, never hold class refs alongside

Option A is simpler given Pascal's object semantics. Option B requires auditing every TDiskBenderDSK.Create call site.
acceptance_criteria: Document chosen model in CLAUDE.md. No site holds both a class-ref and interface-ref to the same instance. Add a regression test that exercises the pattern.
close_reason: Production code already used IVirtualDisk refs throughout; only test code mixed class+interface (fixed earlier this session). Removed the two leftover 'DSK: TDiskBenderDSK' locals in uDSKLocation.pas (RebuildCache, GetSectorMap) — both now use FDisk.GetTrackInfo via the interface. Documented the lifetime convention in CLAUDE.md and saved it as a bd memory.

title: Decouple uCPM from concrete TDiskBenderDSK class
description:
uCPM.pas casts FDisk as TDiskBenderDSK in three hot spots (FindFreeDirEntry, ScanDirectory, GetBlockMap, AddFile, GetFileContent) just to call GetTrackInfo. This breaks the IVirtualDisk abstraction that the rest of the architecture relies on.

Consequence: cannot unit-test the CP/M layer with a mock disk. The recent test_cpm_write.pas had to use a real DSK file and zap its directory to get a clean fixture.

Fix: lift TTrackInfoBlock + GetTrackInfo onto IVirtualDisk (or add IPhysicalDisk interface). Then uCPM uses only interface methods. Then add a TMockVirtualDisk in tests/ that synthesises track layouts in memory.

Files: src/units/uCPM.pas (5 cast sites), src/units/uInterfaces.pas (interface extension), src/units/uDSK.pas (no behaviour change).
acceptance_criteria: uCPM.pas contains zero 'as TDiskBenderDSK' casts. tests/test_cpm_write.pas uses a synthetic in-memory disk instead of /tmp/test_cpm_write.dsk.
close_reason: Lifted GetTrackInfo onto IVirtualDisk; moved TSectorInfo+TTrackInfoBlock to uInterfaces; removed all 7 'as TDiskBenderDSK' casts in uCPM.pas; uCPM no longer uses uDSK at all. Built TMockVirtualDisk in tests/uTestVirtualDisk.pas; test_cpm_write.pas now runs entirely in-memory (no Batman.dsk dependency). 4 write round-trips + 127 TUI tests pass.

title: Resolve dead view-mode state and unused IBlockMappable.GetBlockCount
description:
Code review (2026-05-11) flagged two dead-code items:
1. FViewMode/TViewMode in src/tui/uTUIController.pas is declared+initialised but never read. It is an intentional stub for the brief/full panel-mode feature (CLAUDE.md TODO #7). Add a // TODO #7 comment at the declaration so it is not silent dead state, OR wire it into DrawPane/FormatEntry when the feature lands.
2. IBlockMappable.GetBlockCount (src/units/uVFS.pas) and its TDSKContainer implementation are never called. Either remove the surface (callers use Length(GetBlockMap)) or document why it exists.

Revisit when the view-mode feature is implemented.
notes: FOLLOW-UP (2026-05-14): FViewMode/TViewMode were REMOVED entirely from uTUIController.pas (not just commented). The view-mode toggle feature is deferred until properly designed. IBlockMappable.GetBlockCount retained per the original close reason.
close_reason: Added TODO #7 comment to FViewMode stub; added doc comment to GetBlockCount explaining its retained-for-future-callers status

title: TUI: Hex viewer (F3 on file)
description: F3 currently only toggles disk-block / sector maps. Make it context-aware: when the cursor is on a file (entry implements ICopySource and not IContainer), enter a hex-dump modal mode (tmHex). Otherwise keep existing block/sector-map cycle. Mode shows offset, 16 bytes hex, ASCII gutter; supports Up/Down/PgUp/PgDn/Home/End scrolling; Esc/F3/F10/Q exits. Also add 'Hex view F3' entry to the active-side action menu when an ICopySource entry is selected.
close_reason: Hex viewer (tmHex mode) wired to F3-on-file, F9 menu, scroll/page/home/end nav, Esc/F3/Backspace close, F10/Q exit. Block-allocation map redesigned with 2-char blocks, counts header (Used/Dir/Del/Free with %), row-offset labels, 8-block groups, column ruler, 2-char colored legend. 13 new tests cover hex + map; 149/149 green.

title: Add multi-track directory test fixture (CP/M Plus B-format)
description:
The new FindFreeDirEntry has explicit multi-track-wrap logic for non-CPC formats where DRM>63 spans more than one track. CPC SYSTEM/DATA always fits in 4 sectors of 1 track, so test_cpm_write.pas does not exercise this code path.

Need a fixture or synthetic DSK with DPB equivalent to CP/M Plus B-format (e.g. PCW B-format: DRM=255, dir spans 8 sectors, may straddle a track boundary on small-sector formats). Add a round-trip test that fills the first track of directory, then writes a file requiring an entry in the second track.

Blocked by: DiskBender-77x (decouple uCPM) makes this much easier — synthetic in-memory disk avoids needing a real file.
acceptance_criteria: Test exercises multi-track wrap branch (currently uncovered).
close_reason: Added multi-track wrap to ScanDirectory, GetBlockMap, and FindFreeDirEntry (the latter already had it from earlier work). New regression test: synthetic CPC mock with DPB.DRM=145 (forces 10 dir sectors > 9 sectors/track), pre-fill track 0 dir as 'used', verify AddFile lands the new entry on track 1. Test passes.

title: GetBlockMap: all-space-filename entries falsely mark blocks as live
description:
ScanDirectory creates a synthetic [GUARD] TCPMFile for any directory entry where User<=15 but Filename is all-spaces (defensive recovery for bizarre disk states like the Batman Forever demo). However GetBlockMap then reads those same entries' Allocations bytes and marks every referenced block as 'live' (status=2).

On the Batman demo image this filled every block of the 171-block disk with status≠0, making the disk appear full to the new AddFile allocator. test_cpm_write.pas works around this by zapping the directory to all-$E5 before writing.

Question: are GUARD entries garbage (should be ignored by GetBlockMap) or legit-but-malformed (should keep their blocks)? If garbage, exclude from BlockMap. If legit, AddFile would need a 'force' option for fresh writes.

Files: src/units/uCPM.pas (ScanDirectory:340-352, GetBlockMap:464-513)
acceptance_criteria: Decision documented. GetBlockMap behaviour aligned with that decision. Test demonstrates expected behaviour on Batman.dsk.
notes: SUPERSEDED DECISION (2026-05-11 code review): GetBlockMap now TRUSTS GUARD-entry allocations and shows those blocks as used (state 2), the opposite of this issue's original 'skip GUARD entries' close-reason. Rationale: the block map should be truthful about what space is reserved on copy-protected discs; AddFile correctly refuses on a fully-reserved disc. See CLAUDE.md CP/M Notes and the GetBlockMap comment in src/units/uCPM.pas.
close_reason: Decision: GUARD entries (User<=15 with all-space filename) are directory garbage, not real files. ScanDirectory still surfaces them as [GUARD] for visibility, but GetBlockMap now skips them so their bogus Allocations bytes don't lock up the free pool. New regression test in test_cpm_write.pas: AddFile now succeeds on Batman.dsk WITHOUT zapping the directory — previously failed with 'disk full'.

title: Replace FDPB.SPT div 4 hardcode with TI-derived sectors-per-track
acceptance_criteria: No 'div 4' literal in uCPM.pas. AddFile and GetFileContent both pass through a single helper. Multi-format round-trip test added.
close_reason: Replaced FDPB.SPT div 4 with TI.NumSectors in AddFile and added TI-derived geometry to GetFileContent (was hardcoded /512, /4 for sectors-per-block, sectors-per-track, records-per-sector). Also purged duplicate (FDPB.DRM div (512 div 32)) hardcodes from ScanDirectory, FindFreeDirEntry, and GetBlockMap. Zero geometry literals remain in uCPM.pas. 127 TUI + 5 write tests pass.

title: Support 16-bit block allocation (DSM > 255 formats)
description:
AddFile currently rejects any CP/M format with DSM > 255 because TCPMDirEntry.Allocations is hardcoded as packed array[0..15] of Byte. Larger volumes (CP/M Plus on PCW class C, hard-disk profiles) use 8 × Word allocation entries.

Required changes:
- Discriminate at runtime on FDPB.DSM: 8-bit vs 16-bit allocation
- Read path (GetFileContent, GetBlockMap) currently treats Allocations[B] as Byte — would also need updating
- Round-trip test fixture for a 16-bit-allocation DSK

Impact: blocks compatibility with non-CPC formats. Currently DiskBender silently refuses to import on these; a clear error message should land first as a stopgap.
acceptance_criteria: AddFile and read paths handle 8-bit and 16-bit Allocations correctly. Round-trip test exists for a >256-block format.
close_reason: Added Is16BitAlloc/BlocksPerExtent/GetAllocBlock/SetAllocBlock helpers in TDiskBenderCPM. AddFile no longer refuses DSM>255; uses BlocksPerExt at runtime. GetFileContent and GetBlockMap go through GetAllocBlock so they read 16-bit pointers correctly. Test forces allocation of block 258 (>255) to genuinely exercise the 16-bit path (not coincidentally pass with low block numbers). Round-trip of 2000 bytes matches byte-for-byte.
